behavior_changes: Premium-only discount rate changed from 10% to 15%
New $100 cap on the rounded discount amount
Round-half-up to two decimal places (unchanged, now made explicit)
preserved_invariants: Non-Premium customers (including Student-only) always receive 0% discount

findings.reason: Assertion `result > Decimal('0.00')` passes for both the old 10% and the new 15%. Counterexample: the premium_still_10 mutant returns Decimal('10.00'), which still satisfies > 0.
findings.evidence: baseline suite: PASS on premium_still_10 mutant; evolved suite: BEHAVIORAL_FAIL on same mutant (test_premium_discount_exact_rate asserts == Decimal('15.00'), actual 10.00)
findings.recommended_action: Replace `assert result > Decimal('0.00')` with `assert result == Decimal('15.00')`

findings.reason: Assertion `result > Decimal('0.00')` on a $200 order passes for both 10% ($20) and 15% ($30). Does not constrain the rate.
findings.evidence: baseline suite: PASS on premium_still_10 mutant; evolved test_premium_discount_200 asserts == Decimal('30.00')

findings.test_or_gap: No test in baseline suite covers is_premium=True, is_student=True
findings.reason: The combination case is entirely absent from the baseline suite. There is no baseline assertion that constrains the Premium+Student rate.
findings.evidence: The baseline suite contains no targeted Premium+Student assertion. The evolved suite adds test_premium_and_student_combination, which passes against the correct post-change implementation (Decimal('20.00')). Limitation: the current three-mutant matrix does not include a dedicated mutant for an incorrect Premium+Student rate, so this finding is demonstrated through missing baseline coverage plus the new executable acceptance test, not through a dedicated mutant kill.
findings.recommended_action: Add test: calculate_discount(Decimal('100.00'), is_premium=True, is_student=True) == Decimal('20.00')

findings.test_or_gap: No test in baseline suite for is_premium=False, is_student=True
findings.reason: The preserved invariant — Student-only gets 0% — is never tested. The student_without_premium mutant (grants 20% to non-premium students) passes all 8 baseline tests.
findings.evidence: baseline suite: PASS on student_without_premium mutant (all 8 pass); evolved test_student_only_gets_no_discount catches it: assert Decimal('20.00') == Decimal('0.00')
findings.recommended_action: Add test: calculate_discount(Decimal('100.00'), is_premium=False, is_student=True) == Decimal('0.00')

findings.test_or_gap: No test in baseline suite for order_total that would produce a raw discount > $100
findings.reason: The cap behavior is never exercised. The missing_discount_cap mutant (no cap applied) passes all 8 baseline tests.
findings.evidence: baseline suite: PASS on missing_discount_cap mutant; evolved test_cap_premium_only catches it: assert Decimal('150.00') == Decimal('100.00'); evolved test_rounding_then_cap also catches it: assert Decimal('100.01') == Decimal('100.00')

findings.requirement: Rounding-then-cap behavior (inputs/change-request.md §§3.2–3.4 — calculation order, cap, rounding)
findings.test_or_gap: No rounding-then-cap boundary test in baseline suite
findings.reason: No test verifies that a value which rounds above $100.00 is correctly capped. $666.70 x 15% = $100.005; ROUND_HALF_UP yields $100.01; cap reduces to $100.00.
findings.evidence: Evolved test_rounding_then_cap verifies Decimal('666.70') -> Decimal('100.00') on the correct implementation; missing_discount_cap mutant fails it with Decimal('100.01') != Decimal('100.00')
findings.recommended_action: Add boundary test: calculate_discount(Decimal('666.70'), is_premium=True, is_student=False) == Decimal('100.00')

bob_evidence.description: Bob (Plan mode) read PROJECT_SPEC.md, inputs/change-request.md, sample_app/app/discounts.py, and verification_snapshots/baseline_tests/test_discounts.py. Identified 2 STALE and 4 MISSING findings. No BREAKING findings (baseline passes on correct post-change code).

Bob (Agent mode) tightened 2 stale assertions and created 11 new tests covering Premium+Student combination, Student-only invariant, cap behavior, and rounding-then-cap boundary. Unaffected tests preserved intact.

limitations: This verification measures detection of exactly three chosen, interface-compatible single-defect mutants — not proof the implementation or test suite is complete or correct in general.
No manual-time benchmark was conducted; productivity claims are omitted per spec.

The main controlled scenario has BREAKING = 0 because the baseline suite passes on the correct post-change implementation. The project supports the BREAKING classification conceptually, but no separate BREAKING example was included in the recorded main run.
PDF document reading was not demonstrated; Bob read inputs/change-request.md (Markdown) directly.
Bob session exports are captured as notes in bob_sessions/README.md; IDE screenshots were not committed.

F-003 (Premium+Student coverage) is demonstrated through missing baseline coverage and the new evolved acceptance test. The current three-mutant scope does not include a dedicated mutant for an incorrect Premium+Student rate.
